llm.summary: This is a disclosed China-focused career-planning skill with some optional sharing and follow-up features users should approve explicitly, but I found no hidden execution, exfiltration, or destructive behavior.

dimensions.detail: The default workflow reads bundled reference files and data only. External URLs in datasets are source citations, not active transmissions; optional Tavily, AgentMail, and agent-reach use is gated by user request and host support.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No package install, service install, tool replacement, or startup persistence was found. The only allowed runtime script is the report generator, while the salary database generator is present but not instructed as a runtime path.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The trigger is broad for career questions and the content is primarily Chinese, but that matches the China-focused skill name and description. The top-level instructions repeatedly require explicit user action before networking, email, memory, or follow-up behavior.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The main skill says no default persistence and no default memory writes. Referenced integration and tracker notes describe email delivery, MEMORY.md, and local follow-up files, so users should approve those explicitly and understand retention before enabling them.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The artifacts coherently support career planning with local assessment, salary, industry, and AI-impact references. The insurance-company recommendation module is disclosed and purpose-adjacent, though users should treat it as commercial guidance rather than neutral career data.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Before installing, be comfortable sharing personal career details such as age stage, education, interests, city, and work goals. Do not enable email sending, memory storage, tracking, or real-time search unless you explicitly want those features, and independently verify any insurance-company recommendation or phone contact before acting on it.
llm.findings:
[AE1] expected: The salary database reference is purpose-aligned and the file is present, readable, valid JSON, and contains salary records; the scanner coverage failure was not supported by local inspection.
[SQP-1] expected: Career-planning triggers are broad but aligned with the skill purpose. The insurance path is separately scoped to user insurance interest or insurance-related recommendations.
[SDI-4] expected: The insurance priority recommendation and contact data are disclosed, but the documentation mixes consent-gated contact display with legacy wording that includes a phone number; this is a user-guidance issue, not evidence of hidden behavior.
[SQP-2] expected: Email, memory, and tracking references fit optional report delivery and follow-up workflows, and SKILL.md requires explicit user request before using them. The standalone reference files are terse and should not be treated as default authorization.
[SQP-3] expected: Chinese-language content is expected for a China-focused career planner, and SKILL.md notes multilingual output only on user request.
[E1] expected: The flagged URLs are source_url/source_urls fields in static career and company datasets; I found no instruction or code that sends user data to those URLs.
